name: Betaine aldehyde
description: Betaine aldehyde (CAS 7418-61-3 ) is the direct biosynthetic precursor to betaine, the well-characterized osmoprotectant and methyl donor used across pharmaceutical and nutritional applications. In research and industrial synthesis, it functions as a key intermediate in choline oxidation pathways. This compound bridges choline and betaine in enzymatic and chemical processes, serving as a vital component in metabolic studies. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is used as a building block for producing betaine and related quaternary ammonium compounds in active ingredient manufacturing. Biotechnology and life sciences researchers employ it as a substrate for betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase (BADH) enzyme studies. This makes it a critical reference compound in metabolic pathway research and the development of specialized biochemical assays. In nutritional ingredient production, it supports the synthesis of betaine used in feed additives and dietary supplement formulations. It also serves as a biochemical tool in oxidative stress and methylation research where controlled intermediate availability is critical. Betaine aldehyde is typically supplied as a solution or salt form, most commonly as the chloride salt, reflecting its stability profile in commercial handling. It is available primarily in research and specialty chemical quantities for industrial buyers. Material is supplied to pharmaceutical and biotechnology buyers under documented purity specifications to ensure consistency. Certificates of analysis with HPLC purity data are standard for procurement in regulated research environments and manufacturing sites. The product meets rigorous internal benchmarks and is handled according to industry-standard safety protocols. Suppliers ensure that each batch aligns with the technical requirements necessary for high-stakes laboratory and industrial synthesis applications.
